column3: The verbs “rejoice” and “be glad” are interchanged; “let people say” is rendered “let them say.”
“Thunder” is rendered “roar,” and “what fills it” as “all it contains.”
“Covenant loyalty” is rendered “lovingkindness,” and “for ever” as “everlasting.”
“From antiquity until perpetuity” is rendered “From everlasting even to everlasting.”
“To the matter of a day in its day” is rendered “as every day's work required.”
The Hebrew has “their relatives”; NASB reads “his.” NASB supplies “also,” and the meaning of the repeated name is uncertain.
“To every thing written” is rendered “according to all that is written.”
NASB supplies “with” twice and “should”; “the instruments of the song of God” is rendered “instruments for the songs of God.”
“Went” is rendered “departed,” “turned” as “returned,” and “his house” as “his household.”
